info.title: Quark daemon API
info.description: Local control plane API served by quarkd on localhost.

get.summary:
Every account per harness, with credential health from the harness
adapter and the latest quota reading. A harness with accounts lists its
default account first.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description:
Read every listed account's quota now (one quota-axi call each)
instead of returning the last reading.

post.summary:
Add an account: a config directory for a harness that supports more than
one. Its quota is read right away and arrives as `account.quota_changed`.

409.description: The directory is already an account

get.summary: One account.

delete.summary:
Remove an added account. Its directory is left as it is. Refused for a
default account and while a task runs under the account.

409.description: A default account, or one in use

patch.summary: Rename an added account or replace any account's pools.

get.summary:
A Project coordinator's conversation so far. The coordinator id is the
Project id. New entries arrive as `coordinator.message` events.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only entries with `id` greater than this.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many entries (default and maximum 1000).

post.summary: Send a message to a Project's coordinator.
post.description:
The coordinator id is the Project id. The text is typed into the
coordinator's live session; its reply arrives on the event stream as
`coordinator.message` events, which also carry this message once the
session records it.

409.description: The Project has no workspace yet

get.summary: The decisions inbox across all Projects.

post.description:
The engine records the answer with who gave it, which unblocks the task
that asked. A decision the daemon opened about a rate limit relaunches
the task's worker instead, with the answer as its note. The answered decision is returned and also arrives as a
`decision.answered` event.

502.description: The engine refused or failed the call

get.summary: Typed event stream (WebSocket).
get.description:
Each text frame is one JSON `Event`. Upgrade with a standard WebSocket
handshake; the server ignores client frames other than close.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Last `seq` the client has seen. Every later event is replayed before
live events. Omit to receive only events after connecting; pass 0 to
replay the whole log.

101.description: Switching to WebSocket; each frame is an Event

get.summary:
Every harness the daemon can run, with install state, accepted models
and effort, and credential health for the default account.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: Probe the executables again instead of using the recent result.

post.summary:
Check an agent config before it is saved. Problems come back in the body
with `valid: false`, not as an error status, so a picker can show them.

get.summary: Daemon health and the latest event `seq`.

User-level memory: every entry in the user-level memory directory, by
file name, including files people added by hand.

500.description: `user_memory_failed`: the directory could not be read

get.summary: List Projects.

post.description:
With `repos`, returns at once with status `provisioning` and provisions in
the background: clones the repos into a new Project workspace, writes the
Project repo and starts the coordinator. `project.updated` events report
each step and the final `ready` or `failed` status.

get.summary: Get one Project.

patch.summary: Configure a Project. Absent fields are left unchanged.

409.description: Standing approval needs the Project's workspace

502.description: The engine refused or failed the call

post.summary: Test a task description against the Project's dispatch rules.
post.description:
Runs the engine's dispatch resolution on the description, as the
coordinator does on a task's brief, against the rules `dispatch.yaml` on
the Project repo's `main` declares. Returns the rule the classifier
matched and the profile it would select, or, with no classifier
(`classifier.provider` is `none`), that the coordinator would pick. Every
candidate says whether a worker could start with it now and why: harness
installed, model accepted, account health and quota headroom. Nothing is
dispatched or recorded.

get.summary:
The Project's memory: every entry on the Project repo's `main` under
`memory/`, by path, including files people added by hand. Empty for a
Project without a Project repo.

500.description: `project_repo_failed`: the repo could not be read

get.summary:
A Project repo commit that touched `memory/`, with its diff there: what
an entry's `commit` links to.

parameters.name: commit
parameters.description: Commit id on the Project repo's `main`

500.description: `project_repo_failed`: the repo could not be read

get.summary: A Project's memory proposals, oldest first.
get.description:
A learning a finished task reported becomes a proposal and also arrives
as a `memory.proposed` event.

post.summary: Accept a memory proposal, optionally edited.
post.description:
The entry is written as one new file under the Project repo's `memory/`,
in its own commit on `main`, and the Project's coordinator is told about
it so it reads it on its next turn. The accepted proposal, with its
`entry`, is returned and also arrives as a `memory.accepted` event.

post.summary:
Reject a memory proposal. The rejected proposal is returned and also
arrives as a `memory.rejected` event.
Promote a Project memory entry to user-level memory.
post.description:
The entry is copied as one new file into the user-level memory directory
(`~/.quark/memory/` unless the daemon was started with another), which
every Project's coordinator reads, and each coordinator is told about it.
The Project's own entry stays. Promoting an entry again returns the copy
made the first time.

500.description: `project_repo_failed`, or `user_memory_failed`: the file could not be written

get.summary: The task board for one Project.
Live terminals of one Project: its coordinator and its workers.

post.summary: Retry provisioning a Project whose provisioning failed.
post.description:
Every step is safe to repeat, so provisioning starts again from the first
step. Returns the Project with status `provisioning`.

409.description: The Project is not in a failed state

get.summary:
Pull requests across all Projects, newest first, with their checks and
reviews. Changes arrive as `pr.updated`, `check.updated` and
`review.updated` events.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only pull requests in this state.

get.summary: One pull request.

post.summary: Send a review comment to the worker that owns the pull request.
post.description:
The comment, with its file and line, is durably recorded for the worker
as a steering message; it is not posted on the forge.

409.description: No task owns the pull request, or its workspace is missing

502.description: The engine refused or failed the call

get.summary: The pull request's diff as the forge shows it, or one file of it.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: One file, as named in the diff; absent for the whole pull request.

404.description: Unknown pull request, or a file the diff does not touch

502.description: The forge could not be read

get.summary:
One file a verification gate produced: a Playwright trace, a screenshot,
a video, a log or a report, as listed in the pull request's `evidence`.
get.description:
Served with its content type, `nosniff` and a sandboxing CSP, so an HTML
report cannot run script against the daemon.

404.description: Unknown pull request or artifact, or the file is gone

409.description: No task owns the pull request, or its workspace is missing

post.summary: Merge a pull request through the engine's guarded merge.
post.description:
The engine re-reads the pull request live and refuses unless it is open,
not a draft, free of conflicts and green on its current head. Returns the
pull request as read from the forge after the merge.

409.description: The merge was refused: not green, conflicting, already merged, or no owning task

get.summary: Task detail.

Files the task changed: its working tree, including uncommitted and
untracked work, against where it branched from the default branch.

409.description: The task has no readable working tree

get.summary: Unified diff of the task's changes, or of one changed file.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: One changed file, as listed by `/changes`; absent for the whole task.

404.description: Unknown task, or a path the task did not change

409.description: The task has no readable working tree

get.summary:
Why the task got its agent: one dispatch record per worker spawn, oldest
first (the first spawn, then each relaunch). Empty until the task's worker
has been spawned. Records outlive the task. New records arrive on the
event stream as `dispatch.recorded`.

A task's activity log, oldest first. Live entries arrive on the event
stream as `task.event`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only entries with a greater `id`; 0 or absent starts from the oldest.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many entries (default 200, max 1000).

post.description:
The message is durably recorded for the worker before this returns; the
worker reads it on its next turn.

502.description: The engine refused or failed the call

get.summary:
A worker's transcript so far, read from its harness session log. New
entries arrive as `worker.transcript` events.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only entries with `id` greater than this.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many entries (default and maximum 1000).

post.description:
Stops the worker and keeps its worktree and every uncommitted change;
relaunch picks the task up again.

502.description: The engine refused or failed the call

post.summary: Relaunch a task's worker in the same worktree.

502.description: The engine refused or failed the call

get.summary:
One terminal. Its id is the task id for a worker and the Project id for
a coordinator.

post.summary: Type raw bytes into a terminal.
post.description:
Requests for one terminal are applied in the order they arrive, and HTTP
requests can overtake each other, so keep one request in flight per
terminal and coalesce keys typed meanwhile, or send `seq`.

409.description: `seq` is not after the last applied one

post.summary: Resize a terminal. The last size set wins for every viewer.

post.description:
Appends a `worker.output` snapshot event and returns it. To open a
terminal, subscribe to the event stream, call this, apply the returned
snapshot, then apply the terminal's events with a greater `seq`.

AcceptMemoryProposal.description: Accept a memory proposal, optionally edited.

decided_by.description:
Who is accepting: one line of at most 128 bytes. Absent or null means
the daemon's own user (`$USER`).

text.description: The text to keep instead of the proposed one.

Account.description:
An account a harness runs under: its own config directory, holding what
the harness writes after its own login. Every harness with accounts also
has a default account (`default: true`), its usual config directory, which
is listed but cannot be removed.

active_tasks.description: Tasks and coordinators currently running under the account.

config_dir.description:
The config directory the harness is pointed at (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`,
`CODEX_HOME` and equivalents).

health.description: Credential health from the harness adapter.

id.description: `acc_...`, or `default-<harness>` for a harness's default account.

launchable.description:
False when the engine cannot start this harness under another account
yet, so only its default account can be chosen from a pool.

pools.description:
Pools the account belongs to. A dispatch profile naming a pool runs
each task under one of the pool's accounts for its harness.

AccountFailover.description: One rate limit a task's worker hit, and where the worker went (ADR-11).

at.description: When the daemon handled it (RFC 3339 UTC).

detail.description: What the harness said about the limit, or why the relaunch failed.

from_account_id.description: The account that reported the rate limit (an `Account.id`).

pool.description: The pool the next account was chosen from, when one was named.

signal.description:
The harness log line that reported the limit, e.g.
`claude: assistant isApiErrorMessage error=rate_limit`.

to_account_id.description:
The account the worker was relaunched under; absent unless `outcome`
is `relaunched`.

checked_at.description: When the reading was taken (RFC 3339 UTC).

remaining_percent.description: What limits the account now, 0 to 100.

AgentConfig.description: A harness with its model and effort.

pool.description:
Account pool to run under: one of the harness's accounts in this pool
is chosen per task (see `Account.pools`). Absent runs under the
harness's default account.

AgentConfigValidation.description: The outcome of validating an agent config.

valid.description: True when there are no errors; warnings do not block.

warnings.description: Settings the harness will ignore, e.g. an effort it has no control for.

AgentRole.description: The role an agent plays in a Project.

AnswerDecision.description: An answer to an open decision.

answer.description: The answer, as the worker or coordinator will read it.

answered_by.description:
Who is answering: one line of at most 128 bytes. Stored with the
decision and recorded with the engine's own record of the answer.
Absent or null means the daemon's own user (`$USER`).

AuthState.description: Login or key health for one account.

additions.description: Added lines; absent for binary files.

deletions.description: Removed lines; absent for binary files.

old_path.description: Previous path of a renamed or copied file.

Check.description: One CI check or commit status on a pull request's current head.

conclusion.description: The forge's own conclusion, e.g. `timed_out`, when it says more than `status`.

details_url.description: Link to the run or its log.

name.description: Unique per pull request; for GitHub Actions, `workflow / job`.

CheckStatus.description: The state of one check on a pull request's head.

CheckUpdated.description: Payload of `check.updated`: one check that appeared or changed.

ChecksState.description: One state for all of a pull request's checks on its current head.

ConfigIssue.description: One problem with an agent config.

field.description: The config field the issue is about: `harness`, `model`, `effort` or `role`.

CoordinatorMessage.description: A message for a coordinator, typed into its session as if at the keyboard.

CoordinatorMessageAccepted.description:
The coordinator's session took the message. Its reply arrives as
`coordinator.message` events, read from the session log.

confirmed.description:
`false` when the text was typed and submitted but the session did not
confirm the submit; check the transcript before sending again.

CreateAccount.description: Add an account for a harness.

config_dir.description:
Absolute path of the account's config directory. Log in once with the
harness pointed at it, e.g. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> claude`.

label.description: Shown in the app; defaults to the directory name.

CreateProject.description:
Create a Project.

With `repos`, the daemon provisions it: clones the repos into a new
Project workspace, writes the Project repo and starts the coordinator. The
Project is returned with status `provisioning` and moves to `ready` or
`failed` (see `project.updated` events). `agent_config` is required then.

Without `repos`, the Project is only recorded, optionally attached to an
existing workspace at `workspace_path`.

oneOf.description: One of the presets listed by `DispatchPreset`; default `single`.

workspace_path.description: Attach an existing workspace instead of provisioning one.

Decision.description: A question held for a person.

DeliveryPolicy.description: How a Project's changes reach a pull request.

DiffSide.description: Which side of a diff a line comment is on.

evidence.description:
The quota evidence it was judged on, e.g. `provider=claude
scope=all_models remaining=79%`.

reason.description:
Why it passed or failed, e.g. `eligible` or `profile floor
all_models below 15%`.

detail.description: What was found, e.g. `Claude Code 2.1.0 at /usr/local/bin/claude`.

DispatchChoice.description: The agent a worker was started with.

account.description:
The account the worker was started under (an `Account.id`, as on the
task when it was recorded); absent when the harness has no accounts or
the daemon does not know it.

effort.description: Absent for the harness's default effort.

model.description: Absent for the harness's default model.

DispatchClassifier.description: The classifier behind the System-1 API, as consulted for this dispatch.

confidence.description: The classifier's confidence in the matched rule, from 0 to 1.

provider.description: `none` when no classifier was consulted and the coordinator picked.

DispatchPreset.description:
Starting dispatch rules for a new Project. Both route to the Project's
agent config; rules can be edited afterwards.

DispatchRecord.description:
Why a task got its agent (ADR-11): one record per spawn of the task's
worker. Records are history: they are kept after the task ends, for later
scoring, and never change once recorded.

candidates.description:
Every profile the resolution weighed, in the rule's order, each with
whether it passed and why.

chosen.description: The agent the worker was actually started with.

oneOf.description:
The rate limit this relaunch answered, when the daemon relaunched the
worker to move it to another account; also in `Task.failovers`.

recorded_at.description: When the daemon recorded the dispatch (RFC 3339 UTC).

resolution.description: What the engine's dispatch resolution reported.

oneOf.description:
The dispatch rule the classifier matched; absent when none matched or
no classifier was consulted.

summary.description: One sentence on why this agent, for people.

notes.description: Further notes from the resolution, such as an unranked candidate.

output.description: The resolution's output as the engine printed it, kept for scoring.

DispatchRule.description: A dispatch rule, as the Project's dispatch rules name it.

id.description: The rule's id in the resolution, e.g. `rule_2`, or `default`.

DispatchTest.description:
What a Project's dispatch rules would do with a task description
(ADR-11). Nothing is dispatched or recorded.

candidates.description:
The matched rule's profiles when the resolution weighed them, else
every profile of every rule and the default, in the order the rules
list them.

oneOf.description:
The profile the resolution selected; absent when the coordinator
would pick.

classifier.description:
`provider` is `none` when no classifier is configured and the
coordinator would pick.

decided_by.description:
Who would choose the agent: `classifier` when the resolution selects
a profile, else `coordinator`.

resolution.description: What the engine's dispatch resolution reported for the description.

oneOf.description:
The dispatch rule the classifier matched; absent when none matched or
no classifier is configured.

summary.description: One sentence on the outcome, for people.

DispatchTestCandidate.description:
One profile of the Project's dispatch rules, with whether a worker could
be started with it now.

checks.description: One entry per [`DispatchCheckKind`], in that order.

evidence.description: The quota evidence it was judged on.

pool.description: The account pool the profile runs under, when it names one.

reason.description:
Why it passed or failed: the first failed check, else the
resolution's verdict or `eligible`.

rule.description:
The rule that lists the profile; its id is `default` for a default
profile.

rule_name.description: The rule's `name` in `dispatch.yaml`, when it has one.

Effort.description: Reasoning effort, shared across harnesses. Each harness accepts a subset.

EventType.description:
Every event type the stream can carry. The daemon emits the project, task
and decision events; the rest are reserved so clients can be generated now.

Evidence.description:
Verification gate results for a pull request (ADR-15): repo checks,
Playwright journeys and holdout tests, with traces and screenshots.

head_sha.description: The commit the gates ran on.

stale.description: True when the pull request's head has moved past `head_sha`.

EvidenceArtifact.description: A file a gate produced, served by the daemon.

id.description: Stable for the same file of the same pull request.

FailoverOutcome.description: How a rate limit on a task's account was handled.

FileChangeStatus.description: How a file differs between a task's base and its working tree.

GateCase.description: One case of a gate: a journey, a repo check, or a holdout category.

message.description: Why it failed; absent for holdout cases.

GateKind.description: The verification gates of ADR-15, run in this order before a PR opens.

GateState.description: Where a verification gate, or a case in it, stands.

detail.description: What was checked, e.g. the credential file or environment variable.

HarnessInfo.description: A harness the daemon can run agents with.

account_env.description:
Environment variable that selects an account's config directory, when
the harness supports more than one account.

auth.description: Credential health for the default account.

efforts.description: Accepted effort levels; empty when the harness has no effort control.

id.description: Stable id used in agent configs and dispatch rules, e.g. `claude-code`.

transcript.description: True when chat output can be read from the harness session log.

HarnessInstall.description: Whether a harness is installed on this machine.

install_hint.description: How to install it, shown when it is missing.

version.description: Version string the harness reports, when it could be read.

discovery.description: Where to find the current model list for this harness and account.

source.description: Where busy and turn-end state come from.

engine.description: Name of the engine adapter in use.

last_seq.description: Highest event `seq` in the store; 0 when empty.

MemoryCommit.description: A Project repo commit that touched `memory/`.

patch.description: Unified diff of what it changed under `memory/`.

MemoryEntry.description: One accepted memory entry: a file under the Project repo's `memory/`.

commit.description: The Project repo commit that added it, when known.

date.description:
When it was learned (RFC 3339 UTC); absent for a file written by hand
without one.

id.description: The file name without its extension.

path.description: Path in the Project repo, e.g. `memory/2026-10-02-run-the-gates.md`.

proposal_id.description: The proposal it was accepted from.

files.description:
Files the learning is about: the ones the report names, else the
files the task changed.

pull_request_url.description: The task's pull request when the learning was proposed.

task_id.description: The task it was learned in.

MemoryProposal.description:
A learning from a finished task, waiting for review before it becomes
Project memory.

oneOf.description: The entry it became, once accepted.

text.description: The text as proposed, or as accepted when it was edited.

MemorySource.description: Where a memory proposal came from.

MergeMethod.description: How to merge a pull request.

MergePullRequest.description: Request body for `POST /v1/pull-requests/{id}:merge`; may be empty.

oneOf.description: Default `squash` on GitHub; GitLab uses the project's own setting.

Mergeability.description: Whether the forge can merge the head into the base without conflicts.

ModelSelection.description: How a harness chooses its model.

Project.description: A Project: a goal-driven workspace that owns tasks, decisions and PRs.

oneOf.description: Harness, model and effort the coordinator and, by default, workers use.
Dispatch preset the Project's `dispatch.yaml` was created from.

project_repo_path.description:
Local path of the Project repo (bare), which holds `project.yaml`,
`dispatch.yaml`, `instructions.md` and `memory/`.

repos.description: Code repos in the Project workspace.

standing_approval.description:
Merge this Project's pull requests as soon as they are green, without
asking. Maps to the engine's merge posture for the Project's repos.

status_detail.description: What is happening now while provisioning, or why provisioning failed.

workspace_path.description: Local path of the Project workspace, once it is provisioned or attached.

ProjectStatus.description: Where a Project is in its lifecycle.

PromoteMemoryEntry.description: Promote a Project memory entry to user-level memory.

PullRequest.description:
A pull request opened by one of a Project's tasks, with its checks and
reviews as last read from the forge.

oneOf.description: Verification gate results (ADR-15); absent until the gates report.

head_sha.description: Head commit the checks and mergeability refer to.

opened_at.description: When the forge reports the PR was opened, updated, merged and closed.

sync_error.description: Why the last forge read failed, until one succeeds.

synced_at.description: When the daemon last read the forge successfully.

title.description: Absent until the forge has been read.

PullRequestComment.description:
A review comment for the worker that owns the pull request. It is
delivered to the worker as a steering message, not posted on the forge.

path.description: File the comment is about, as it appears in the diff.

PullRequestDiff.description: A unified diff of a pull request, or of one of its files.

path.description: The file this diff covers; absent for the whole pull request.

truncated.description: True when `patch` was cut at the size limit.

PullRequestState.description: Where a pull request is in its life.

QuotaState.description: Whether an account's quota could be read.

QuotaWindow.description: One rate-limit window of an account's plan.

RelaunchTask.description:
Replace a task's worker in the same worktree. Absent fields keep the
worker's current harness, model and effort.

note.description:
Where things stand, for the new worker, which keeps the worktree but
none of the conversation. A default note is used when absent.

pool.description:
Account pool to choose from when the task has no usable account of
the harness yet; absent uses the Project agent config's pool when the
harness matches. A task keeps its account across relaunches.

RepoSource.description: A forge repo in a Project workspace.

name.description: Short name, unique in the Project; derived from the URL when absent.

url.description: Clone URL (https, ssh, scp-like or an absolute local path).

commit.description: Head commit the review was left on.

ReviewDecision.description: What reviewers decided, as the forge sums it up.

ReviewUpdated.description: Payload of `review.updated`: one review that appeared or changed.

SendTaskMessage.description: A steering message for a task's worker.

text.description: Plain text for the worker to read; may span several lines.

SupervisionConfidence.description: How confidently the daemon can tell when an agent is busy or done.

account_id.description:
The account the task's worker was started under (an `Account.id`),
when the harness has accounts.

failovers.description:
Each time the worker hit a rate limit, oldest first: the account it
moved to, or why it could not move.

state_note.description: Short human-readable note about the latest state change.

TaskChanges.description:
Files a task changed: its working tree, including uncommitted and
untracked work, compared with where it branched from the default branch.

base.description: Commit the task branched from (merge base with `base_ref`).

base_ref.description: The default-branch ref the task is compared against, e.g. `origin/main`.

head.description: Commit checked out in the task's working tree.

TaskDiff.description: A unified diff for a whole task or one of its files.

path.description: The file this diff covers; absent for the whole task.

truncated.description: True when `patch` was cut at the size limit.

TaskEvent.description:
One entry of a task's activity log: something the worker or the engine
reported about the task. History, not current state; the task's `state`
is the reconciled truth.

decision_key.description: The decision this entry opens or closes, when it names one.

id.description: Monotonic per daemon; pass the last one seen as `after` to page.

ts.description: When the daemon read the entry (RFC 3339 UTC).

TaskState.description:
Neutral task lifecycle state. Engine adapters map their own states onto
these; anything they cannot classify is `unknown`.

Terminal.description: A live terminal: one session pane the daemon streams as `worker.output`.

id.description: The task id for a worker, the Project id for a coordinator.

TerminalInput.description: Raw bytes to type into a terminal.

data_b64.description:
Base64 of the bytes, exactly as a terminal would send them
(`\r` for Enter, escape sequences for keys).

seq.description:
Optional per-terminal sequence number. When given, it must be greater
than the last one applied, so a retried request is not typed twice.

TestDispatch.description: A task description to test against a Project's dispatch rules.

description.description: The task as it would be briefed to a worker.

TranscriptEntry.description:
One entry of a coordinator or worker transcript, parsed from the harness's
own session log. Payload of `coordinator.message` and `worker.transcript`.

text.description:
Markdown for `user`, `assistant` and `thinking`; tool input or output
otherwise.

tool_name.description: Tool name, for `tool_call` and `tool_result` when the harness records it.

truncated.description: `true` when `text` was cut to the daemon's size limit.

ts.description: RFC 3339 timestamp recorded by the harness, when present.

id.description:
The `seq` of the event that carried this entry; pass it as `after` to
page, and use it to merge history with live events.

TranscriptItem.description: A transcript entry as listed by the history endpoints.

TranscriptRole.description: Who or what produced a transcript entry.

UpdateAccount.description: Partial update; absent fields are left unchanged.

label.description: Not accepted for a default account.

UpdateProject.description: Partial update; absent fields are left unchanged.

standing_approval.description:
Turn standing approval on or off. Needs the Project's workspace when
the Project has repos.

UserMemoryEntry.description:
One entry of user-level memory: a file under `~/.quark/memory/`, which
every Project's coordinator reads. A file written by hand carries only
`id`, `path` and `text`.

commit.description: The Project repo commit that added that entry, when known.

entry_id.description: The Project memory entry it was promoted from.

id.description: The file name without its extension.

path.description: Absolute path of the file on this machine.

project_id.description: The Project it was promoted from.

oneOf.description: The role the config is for; absent checks it as a worker.
